name: dns-san-trailing-dot-invalid
description: permittedSubtrees is dNSName 'example.com' (no trailing dot, the conformant form). The leaf SAN encodes the dNSName with a trailing root-label dot ('www.example.com.'). RFC 5280 4.2.1.6 says dNSName SANs SHOULD NOT include a trailing dot — the value is supposed to be the preferred-name-syntax form, not a fully-qualified DNS query name — so a strict validator rejects the SAN at parse time. Independently, a byte-wise subtree match against the constraint 'example.com' fails because the trailing-dot string isn't a suffix of the constraint form. Validators that strip trailing dots before comparison normalise the leaf to 'www.example.com' and then incorrectly accept it.
notes: Constructed via unknown_extensions because cryptography.x509.DNSName rejects the trailing dot before the cert is built.
This complements `dns-constraint-trailing-dot-invalid` (which puts the trailing dot on the constraint side); here the leaf is the malformed side and the constraint is conformant.
